source: Royal Government of Cambodia, General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), "ខែ្សសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំពោតនៅកម្ពុជា" (Corn Production Value Chain in Cambodia), 2017
text:
Cambodia exports substantial volumes of surplus corn, mainly across the land border into Vietnam and, from western provinces, into Thailand. Over roughly 200,000 tons of corn per year has historically been exported this way (cited to Barrientos 2017b). Export volume and quality (moisture control) have been improving over the last several years. Cambodia's government has facilitated corn exports, importing about 130,000 tons' worth of trade opportunity in 2017 (per Cheng, 2017). Corn export prices at the border were reported around 200 to 230 US dollars per ton (Cheng, 2017).

Recently, China's government has also begun actively seeking to import corn from Cambodia, similar to its approach with other Cambodian crops. As of the source's writing, Cambodia had exported about 70,487 tons of corn to China (as of 2016), a 25% increase from 2015, though this was still only about 65% of the volume Cambodia exported to Vietnam that year.

Cambodia has also brought in roughly 7,728 tons of imported corn worth about 3.69 million US dollars in one recent year (2016, per Cheng 2017), up 36% from 2015's 319 tons worth about 40,000 US dollars -- a sharp jump attributed largely to increased need for imported corn by domestic feed processors during periods when domestic supply was tight or price/quality did not match feed-mill needs.
